name: Brinemaster Ogo
bio: Third Brinemaster of Saltmouth and keeper of the master ledgers. Built the Guild's water monopoly and sleeps badly because of it. Wants the null crate archived, shelved, or sold — anything except listened to. Genuinely fond of couriers, which he expresses by underpaying them slightly less.
appearance: Broad, weathered man in a long ochre coat stiff with salt at the hem, a brass scale-pin at his collar, white beard cropped square like a ledger margin, and rings on every finger — each one a closed contract.
voice: Avuncular menace. Speaks in brine and measure metaphors; everything is a weight, a price, or a debt. Never threatens directly — he quotes policy. Laughs harder the less funny things get.

greetings: Courier Varga. Sit. No, don't sit, the chair's rented.
Ash Varga, the debt that walks like a person. Come in, come in.
Everything crosses. Everything's counted. You're counted among my favourite expenses.
barks: A sealed crate is a sleeping dog. We do not wake dogs, we sell them.
I have weighed kingdoms in salt, child. They are always lighter than the paperwork.
Change is corrosion. Profit is preservation. Choose your chemistry.
mission: The Guild's offer is simple: the crate goes into deep archive, your debt goes into shallow archive, and we all pretend the desert doesn't hum.
Sign the custody transfer and your ledger loses three zeroes of ugly. I am, at heart, a romantic.
radio: Brinemaster Ogo on Guild band one. Courier, your altitude is billable. Descend at your leisure, billing continues.
I am told the crate hums. I have in my office forty crates that hum. They are called bees. We insure bees.
Remember, Varga: the Guild doesn't fear the future. We simply invoice it until it calms down.
night: The ledgers balance differently after dark. Less honestly. Like everyone.
Night tariffs apply, courier. Not to goods. To hopes.
storm: Storm season is the desert's audit season. We all show our books or lose them.
Wall of sand on the scope, Varga. The Guild advises stillness. The Guild is a building.
crate: That crate has no weight in any ledger I own, and I own the concept of ledgers.
Bring me the crate and I'll call your debt a rounding error. I have never once permitted a rounding error. Think on what you're being offered.
farewells: Flat salt, courier. The counting continues without you. It always does.
Go. And remember: I liked you slightly before everyone else did. There'll be a fee.
